comments.author: laxmareddyp
comments.body:
Hi @sowmya04101998 ,

Same as legacy code you can configure the yaml file and pass it to the trainer.py. For image_classification experiment you can run as below.
python3
python3 official/vision/train.py \
    --experiment=image_classification\
    --mode=train_and_eval\
    --model_dir=/tmp/trained_model/ \
    --config_file=pramas.yaml

params.yaml file should have configuration for multi-worker gpu that you have configured and proper architecture that your model is going to be trained on. For example take a look at this [config](https://github.com/tensorflow/models/blob/master/official/vision/configs/experiments/image_classification/imagenet_mobilenetv2_gpu.yaml) file which is for gpu mirrored strategy. If you still cannot run train.py ,Please share the error so that we can look into it further. I hope this helps to get some insight to train the model.

Hi @sowmya04101998,

I guess you are cloning repo and trying to use train.py and also have installed pip install tf-models-official==2.11.0 which doesn't have latest code changes of git clone. So if you are using cloned repo make sure to follow this process.

consider this as nightly because you are using latest master branch
bash
$ git clone -q https://github.com/tensorflow/models.git
$ pip install -q -U tensorflow==2.13.0
$ pip install -q -U tensorflow_datasets
$ pip install -q --user -r models/official/requirements.txt
$ pip install -q -U tensorflow-text
Pip install official models which doesn't require you to clone repo for using official code.
bash
$ pip install -U tf-models-official

follow one of the above not both.


Now train the model as done in the [notebook](https://colab.research.google.com/gist/sineeli/e52ecd82a10d82f4955ef7f333ab6b3c/-11042.ipynb):


I have downgraded pip because latest release of Cython having some issue while install tf-models-official. Notebook only showcases single GPU but it can be used for single machine multi gpu. But to use multi-machine multi gpu, the yaml file configuration will be different, rest of the steps should be same.

This notebook shows how to train the model using official.vision.train file or else you can train without using train.py file way which is explained in the notebook here:

[Image Classification Example](https://www.tensorflow.org/tfmodels/vision/image_classification)
[Object Detection Example](https://www.tensorflow.org/tfmodels/vision/object_detection)

this notebooks will help you to train end to end with latest official code. Please let us know if this helps you understand.

comments.author: laxmareddyp
comments.body:
Hi @sowmya04101998,

Would you mind trying to create the environment I provided in the notebook above and running it? This environment uses the latest tf-models-officials code, instead of the legacy code you are currently using. We do not support the legacy code base, and we encourage everyone to use the latest official code.

To create the environment as described in the notebook and utilize the latest tf-models-official code, Before installing tf-models-official, please make sure to install the specific version 5.3.1 of PyYAML. There have been some reported issues with the latest release version of PyYAML, so it's essential to use version 5.3.1.

You can install PyYAML version 5.3.1 with the following command: `pip install PyYAML==5.3.1`

Once you have installed PyYAML version 5.3.1, you can proceed to install the latest version of tf-models-official using the following command:`pip install tf-models-official`

If you follow the setup above, it should not throw any errors, as we expect.

Thanks.
